description: Shows finished jobs so a homeowner can judge quality before calling: project portfolios, single-job case studies, before/after comparisons and progress sequences. On a trade site it is the main proof section, so photos lead and every job says what was done and where.
queries: before and after image comparison slider
case study section with project photos and results
construction and renovation company recent projects section
home renovation before and after photos section

references.layout: Full-bleed project photo (~100vw x ~70vh) with the project name centered on it in white. Directly below, a solid peach band split roughly 1/3 + 2/3: the left column holds four short metadata lines (Category / Conducted / Location / Involvement), the right column a large intro paragraph (~4 lines). No cards, no buttons in view.
references.type: Title in an ultra-condensed grotesk (Bebas/Druk-like), uppercase, ~56px, tight tracking. Intro paragraph sans ~20px regular, line-height ~1.35. Metadata sans ~12px regular as plain 'Label: value' lines.
references.color: Photo-driven top; white title; peach band ~#fde0d2; text ~#111. Site utility bar above is signal yellow ~#ffe000.
details: Metadata written as plain 'Category: Hotel / Conducted: 2023 / Location: Palma' lines with no icons
Huge size jump between the ~12px metadata and the ~20px intro creates hierarchy without bold
Title sits directly on a mid-tone photo with no gradient scrim
Peach band color is pulled from the warm stone in the photo
references.why_it_works: It treats one job like a magazine feature. The metadata answers what, when and where in two seconds, and the intro paragraph tells the story.
references.trade_adaptation: Single-job page for a remodeler or roofer: photo of the finished kitchen or roof, title 'HOLLIS AVE KITCHEN', meta lines 'Service: Full remodel / Completed: May 2025 / Location: Westfield / Duration: 6 weeks', intro paragraph in the owner's words about the problem and the fix.

references.layout: Centered header: tiny grey pill 'Featured reviews', then a 2-line heading (~30px) whose second line is in a tan accent. Below, a horizontal carousel of pale grey cards (~220px wide, ~16px radius) that bleed off both viewport edges. Each card: amber result pill at top, two side-by-side photos (~80x120, ~8px radius) captioned 'Month 0' / 'Month 7' underneath, then a centered 4-5 line quote.
references.type: Geometric sans. Heading ~30px regular, line 2 recolored. Result pill ~9px medium. Photo captions ~10px grey. Quote ~14px regular, centered, curly quotes.
references.color: White page; cards ~#f4f4f4; pill fill amber ~#f6c27a with dark brown text ~#5a3b00; accent heading line tan ~#c98a4b; body ~#222.
details: Result pill states the outcome with a timeframe ('34 lbs lost in 7 months')
Photos labeled with time stamps instead of the words Before/After
Cards cropped at both viewport edges signal swipe without arrows
Quote sits under the photos so the evidence comes first
references.why_it_works: Three kinds of proof in one card: paired photos, a quantified result and a human quote. The time labels make the change feel real rather than staged.
references.trade_adaptation: Painter, cleaner, landscaper or roofer: pill 'Full tear-off in 3 days', photos labeled 'Day 1' / 'Day 3' (or 'Before' / 'After'), homeowner quote and town underneath. Photos must be shot from the same angle for the pairing to read.

references.layout: 3x2 grid, ~16px gutters, ~48px between rows. Each card is an image tile (~3:2, ~10px radius) with a white uppercase micro-label overlaid top-left ('SAVED $30K+', '10+ CLIENT PROJECTS', '700+ PROJECTS'), and a 2-3 line headline sentence below the tile. No buttons; the whole card is the link.
references.type: Headline sans medium ~15px, line-height ~1.3, black. Overlay labels in a mono-ish uppercase ~10px with ~0.08em tracking.
references.color: White page; tiles mix photography with flat fills (black ~#000, sage ~#5c8a5a, navy gradient); labels white; headlines ~#111.
details: The metric is the eyebrow: result first, story second
Headlines are 'How X did Y' sentences, not project titles
No 'Read more' link; the card itself is clickable
Overlay label sits on the image corner with no backing chip
references.why_it_works: Leading with a number turns each project into evidence, and the sentence headline tells you why to click.
references.trade_adaptation: Roofer or HVAC grid of job photos with overlay labels like '2-DAY TEAR-OFF', '$0 CHANGE ORDERS', '40-YR WARRANTY'; headline 'How the Delgados stopped a 30-year leak before winter'. Use real job photos only; skip the logo-on-color tiles.

references.layout: Wide grid with deliberately mixed tile sizes per row: row 1 = one large landscape tile (~half width) + two small; row 2 = small square, large centered landscape, small; row 3 = large + two small. Tiles share a top line per row but bottoms vary. Tiny control bar above: 'View: Image / List' toggle and 'Filter by: Categories (16)'. Each tile has a two-line caption under it.
references.type: Neo-grotesk (Helvetica-like) at small sizes only: client name ~12px medium black, tagline ~11px regular grey. No section heading; images carry it.
references.color: White ~#fff, text ~#111, taglines ~#777. All color comes from the photography.
details: Image/List view toggle gives a text index of the same work
Category count in parentheses '(16)'
Row gaps (~60px) are much larger than gutters (~16px), so rows read as spreads
Captions are always one line: name plus a short tagline
references.why_it_works: Tile size does the ranking: the strongest job gets the biggest tile. It looks curated rather than templated.
references.trade_adaptation: Remodeler or roofer portfolio: hero job in the large tile, detail shots (flashing, tile work, trim) in small tiles; caption 'Cedar shake re-roof, Maplewood'; filters by service (Roofing / Gutters / Siding); List view as a job log.

references.layout: Uniform 3-column grid, ~16px gutters, ~3:2 landscape images with square corners; caption block under each image (bold title + 1-3 line description); ~50px between rows. A full-width-ish pale grey 'Load more +' bar (~370px wide, ~28px tall) centered below the grid.
references.type: Sans (Graphik-like). Title ~13px medium ~#1a1a1a; description ~12px regular ~#6b6b6b, line-height ~1.35. Button label ~10px.
references.color: White page, near-black titles ~#1a1a1a, grey descriptions ~#6b6b6b, load-more fill ~#ececec.
details: Each description says what was done in one sentence
No cards, borders or shadows: the image edge is the grid
Understated 'Load more +' instead of a loud CTA
Consistent image ratio keeps the grid calm even with busy photos
references.why_it_works: Disciplined and photo-first. The restraint makes ordinary work look expensive.
references.trade_adaptation: Painter or remodeler project grid: 'Victorian exterior repaint' + 'Full prep, three-color scheme, 9 days.' Load more for dozens of jobs without a separate page.

references.layout: Hairline at top, then a control row: 'FILTER:' + pills (ALL filled black; BRAND / MARKETING / PRODUCT grey) on the left, 'DISPLAY:' STACK/GRID toggle on the right. A 2-line statement headline spans the width. Below, a featured image card (~65% width, ~16px radius) on the left and a smaller card (~33%) on the right with caption: client ~11px, 2-line headline ~15px, hashtag tag.
references.type: Statement in a narrow serif (~36px regular, tight tracking). Captions neutral sans; filter labels and tags in mono uppercase ~9px.
references.color: White ~#fff; active pill ~#111 with white text; inactive pills ~#e8e8e8; text ~#111 / ~#666.
details: A sentence about the work replaces the 'Our Work' heading
Tags written as '#MARKETING' in mono
Stack/Grid display toggle
Rounded corners (~16px) only on images, never on text blocks
references.why_it_works: One big featured job plus a smaller supporting one gives the section a lead story, and the serif statement sets the voice.
references.trade_adaptation: Landscaper: statement 'Gardens built to outlast the people who planted them.' Featured card = biggest backyard install; filters Hardscape / Planting / Irrigation.

references.layout: Text-only index. Top-left 'All projects' with a superscript count (43); top-right a 4-line intro paragraph. Below, a 3-column list with no rules: project name (~50% width), sector, 'City, Country'. Rows ~20px tall with ~6px spacing; 10+ rows visible.
references.type: Neo-grotesk ~14px regular for everything, one weight; superscript count ~8px.
details: Superscript project count next to the label
No images, borders or icons; reads like a ledger
Location column on every row
Columns align to the same grid as the intro paragraph above
references.why_it_works: Volume is the proof. A long, plain list of real jobs and places reads more confident than a few hero shots.
references.trade_adaptation: Plumber or electrician 'Job log': 'Tankless water heater install / Plumbing / Cranford, NJ'. 40+ rows prove local track record; each row can link to photos. Pairs well with a photo grid above.

references.layout: Horizontal rail of near-square tiles (~250x280, ~4px radius, ~12px gaps); first tile cut at the left edge, last at the right. Two-line caption under each: project name, then (client) in parentheses. Footer row: 'Clients - 2013/2024' left, '(Scroll)' right. Header shows the studio's city and local time.
references.type: Neutral grotesk ~11px regular black for captions and footer; nav ~11px.
references.color: White page, near-black text ~#111, full-saturation imagery.
details: Parenthetical '(Scroll)' hint instead of arrow buttons
Local time and city in the header ('Toronto, Canada 4:50 am')
Client name in parentheses on the second caption line
Tiles bleed off both edges to imply more
references.why_it_works: Low chrome lets the images carry the section; the place-and-time detail quietly says 'we are local and open'.
references.trade_adaptation: Electrician or HVAC: rail of recent installs captioned 'Panel upgrade (Hendricks residence)'; header line 'Westfield, NJ 7:42 am, crews out now'.

references.layout: Large photo on the left (~40% width, ~400px tall) with an italic caption beneath. To its right, a filmstrip of ~7 small thumbnails (~60x75) bottom-aligned to the main image's baseline, each with a year label below (2023, 2024, 2025, 2026). Top-right counter '1 / 12' and 'NEXT'.
references.type: Small sans ~9px for labels and counter; caption italic ~9px.
references.color: Warm off-white ~#fbf8ee page, black text ~#111, natural photo colors.
details: Date stamps under thumbnails turn photos into a timeline
Thumbnails share the main image's bottom edge
Plain '1 / 12' counter instead of dots
Italic caption describes what the photo shows
references.why_it_works: A sequence of dated photos tells a story of progress, which is exactly what a renovation is.
references.trade_adaptation: Job progress gallery: main photo = finished roof or kitchen; filmstrip labeled 'Day 1 tear-off', 'Day 2 decking', 'Day 3 shingles', 'Final walkthrough'. Counter shows photo count.

references.layout: Solid olive field, full-bleed. Three photo cards (~150x160, ~4px radius) placed in a staggered, non-grid arrangement. Each card has a square badge top-left with a big number ('8 T/HA', '56 T/HA', '↑27.5%'), and bottom-left a white title ('Wheat') plus a tiny uppercase result caption.
references.type: Sans throughout. Badge numbers ~22px medium white with unit underneath ~10px; titles ~14px; captions uppercase ~7px, tracked.
references.color: Olive field ~#5b6f35; badges a lighter olive ~#6f8a3c; white text; natural photo colors.
details: Badge color matches the background, so cards look cut out of the field
Staggered placement instead of a grid
Uppercase micro-captions carry real figures and dates
Arrow glyph in the metric ('↑27.5%') signals improvement
references.why_it_works: Organic placement plus hard numbers feels both handmade and credible.
references.trade_adaptation: Landscaper or lawn care on a deep green field: cards 'Lawn renovation, 90% coverage in 6 wks', 'Drainage regrade, zero standing water', with a square badge for the number.

references.layout: Tall single-project spread. Photos (~4:5 and ~3:2 mixed) staggered left and right in a 2-column offset rhythm with ~40px vertical offsets. The serif title sits in the empty top-right column instead of above the photos. Each photo has a tiny caption under it.
references.type: Serif ~16px light for the 2-line title; captions sans ~7px grey ('Photo: Emanuel Bougot').
references.color: White page, black type, warm wood and neutral interior photography.
details: Photo credit and subject in each caption
Title fills a gap in the stagger rather than taking its own row
No two photos share a top edge
Lots of white space; the photos breathe
references.why_it_works: Magazine pacing makes one project feel like a story, which suits craft trades with detail work.
references.trade_adaptation: Single-project page for a carpenter or remodeler: staggered shots of built-ins with captions 'Walnut built-ins, living room' and a serif title 'The Hollis Street library' in the gap.

references.layout: Deep blue band. Mono eyebrow 'WHAT HOMEOWNERS SAY' top-left, serif headline below ('Real homes. Real savings.'). Three equal portrait cards (~210x320, ~10px radius), each a photo of the customer's house with a frosted-glass panel covering ~85% of it, holding a large quote and 'Name, Town' at the bottom.
references.type: Transitional serif for headline (~36px light) and quotes (~20px light), white. Eyebrow mono uppercase ~8px. Attribution sans ~9px.
references.color: Royal blue ~#2b4aa0 band; white text; frosted panels ~rgba(255,255,255,0.15) with background blur.
details: The customer's own house is the background of each quote
Frosted glass keeps the house visible behind the words
Attribution includes town and state ('Norwood, MA')
Mono eyebrow vs serif headline pairing
references.why_it_works: Joins project photo and review in one object: proof the house exists and the owner is happy.
references.trade_adaptation: Roofing, solar or HVAC: photo of the actual finished roof behind 'Our energy bill dropped 30%', signed 'Sarah M., Cranford'. Works as a bridge between gallery and testimonials.

takeaways: Photos lead and captions stay short: what was done + where (+ when). One line beats a paragraph; ~11-13px captions under images with no card chrome.
Rank work by size: one featured job larger than the rest (mixed tile sizes or a featured card + smaller card) instead of a uniform grid of equals.
Put a result on the card: an overlay eyebrow or pill with a number and timeframe ('2-DAY TEAR-OFF', 'Restored in 3 days').
Before/after works best as paired photos from the same angle, labeled with time ('Day 1' / 'Day 3'), plus a result pill and a homeowner quote.
Every project names its town. Location metadata is both trust and local SEO, and it is what homeowners scan for.
Give volume a home: a plain text job index or List view proves track record without 40 photos.
Single-job pages: full-bleed finished photo, then a metadata band (Service / Completed / Location / Duration) and an intro paragraph.
Keep chrome minimal: ~16px gutters, ~48-64px row gaps, no shadows or borders; color comes from photos or one full-bleed brand band.
avoid: Generic 3-column cards with drop shadows, a stock photo, a pink/blue headline and a 'Read case study >' link on every card (Toggl Track, Superhuman, Voiceflow style).
Logo-on-gradient or 'Brand VS Brand' tiles instead of real photos of the work (Kajabi comparisons, Contra's logo tiles).
3D arc, fanned or stacked-deck carousels (Inkwell) that hide the photos and break on phones.
Dark, scroll-jacked, drag-to-explore galleries with hover-only titles (Studio Freight, Freshman): unreadable for a homeowner on a phone.
Text-only 'Before / With us' columns with ✕ and ✓ bullets (V7, Cake Equity, Contractbook): SaaS shorthand; trades need photo pairs.
Lazy-loaded galleries that render blank without JS (several results captured as empty grey frames).
Purple-glow gradients and blurred 'unlock' metrics as decoration.
